```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
library(readfiscalau)
source("_helpers.R")
chart_chunk <- c(
  "_chart-example.R",
  file.path("vignettes", "_chart-example.R"),
  file.path("..", "vignettes", "_chart-example.R")
)
chart_chunk <- chart_chunk[file.exists(chart_chunk)]
if (length(chart_chunk) < 1L) {
  stop(
    "Chart chunk not found; cwd=", getwd(), "; candidates=",
    paste(c("_chart-example.R", file.path("vignettes", "_chart-example.R"),
            file.path("..", "vignettes", "_chart-example.R")), collapse="|")
  )
}
read_chart_chunk <- knitr::read_chunk
read_chart_chunk(chart_chunk[[1L]])
```

`readfiscalau` reads selected, schema-governed Australian Commonwealth fiscal
publications. The shortest reliable workflow is:

1. inspect the local manifest and lightweight search controls;
2. choose a supported release/resource row;
3. read it with the typed reader for its release type; and
4. retain the provenance attribute with the returned tibble.

This vignette uses packaged replay fixtures for the data read, so it does not
need network access and does not depend on a changing government endpoint.

## Sources and coverage

The package uses publications from three Australian Government sources:

| Publisher | Main workflow | Current admitted coverage |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [Australian Treasury](https://budget.gov.au/) | Budget and MYEFO vintage tables, FBO historical aggregates, and Budget archive discovery | Budget vintages 2000–01 to 2026–27; MYEFO vintages 2000–01 to 2025–26. The pinned FBO history contains annual actual aggregates from 1970–71 to 2024–25. The archive catalogue spans 1901–02 to 2026–27 and is discovery/preservation metadata, not chart-ready observations. |
| [Department of Finance](https://www.finance.gov.au/publications/commonwealth-monthly-financial-statements) | Monthly financial statement aggregates and CKAN metadata | Archived statement PDFs begin in January 2000. The machine-readable aggregates used by the package begin in July 2000 and currently run through May 2026. Finance supplies July–May; Treasury FBO data can complete June. |
| [Parliamentary Budget Office](https://www.pbo.gov.au/publications-and-data/data-and-tools/data-portal/historical-fiscal-data) | Structured forecast workbooks used for selected Budget/MYEFO observations, plus a separate table-oriented historical reader | Historical-table coverage is table-specific: Table 9 AGS debt starts in 1900–01; Table 6 cash receipts in 1901–02; Table 8 cash flow in 1953–54; Table 7 expenses in 1964–65; Tables 1 and 2 aggregates in 1970–71; other tables start later. Budget/MYEFO panel coverage is described below. |

The ranges describe data surfaced by this package release, not every document
held by each publisher.

### Finance monthly statements

Finance's archive includes monthly-statement PDFs from
[January 2000](https://www.finance.gov.au/archive-link/australian-government-general-government-sector-monthly-financial-statements-january-2000),
but the [machine-readable aggregates workbook](https://data.gov.au/data/en/dataset/australian-government-general-government-sector-monthly-financial-statements-tables-and-data/resource/1e1e039e-c54d-4c59-973b-7b15cde2ed63)
used by the package begins in fiscal year 2000–01. Its first observation is
July 2000, which is the starting point of
`read_au_monthly_financial_history()`; the package does not parse the earlier
2000 PDFs.

Finance supplies July–May YTD observations. The reader derives monthly flows,
keeps stocks as month-end levels, and can add June from a compatible annual FBO
release. Cash measures such as receipts, payments, and cash balances remain
separate from accrual measures such as revenue, expenses, and balance-sheet
items. A material format and accounting boundary at 2008–09 remains explicit
through `accounting_basis`, `accounting_framework`, source labels, and
`schema_family`; historical values are not recast across that boundary.

### Budget and MYEFO publication-vintage data

The installed historical-table snapshot covers 22 economically and fiscally
material table families across all 28 Budgets from 2000–01 to 2026–27 and all
25 MYEFOs from 2000–01 to 2025–26. It is a static RDS built from official
Treasury PDFs, so user queries are local and do not reparse a PDF. The selected
families cover economic forecasts; headline cash/accrual and balance-sheet
aggregates; detailed receipts and reconciliations; expenses and investment;
debt and interest; and formal sector financial statements.

```{r budget-myefo-family-overview}
historical_families <- list_au_budget_myefo_families()
historical_families[, c(
  "family_label", "query_mode",
  "budget_first_vintage", "myefo_first_vintage"
)][1:8, ]
```

Use `list_au_budget_myefo_families()` for all 22 family-level coverage rows and
`list_au_budget_myefo_series()` for series-specific periods, and
`list_au_budget_myefo_series_profiles()` for exact non-duplicating application
paths. Durable concepts
have canonical IDs across duplicate source tables; variable reconciliation
detail is retrieved as a complete table. Aggregate `Total` columns and source
charts are not promoted to series. The dedicated
[historical Budget and MYEFO tables](budget-myefo-table-history.html) article
documents the complete map and examples.

The existing curated high-level panels remain available without behavior
changes. They surface selected table families from each publication:

| Panel | Publication vintages | Selected table families | Observation envelope across all admitted series |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Budget | 28 vintages, 2000–01 to 2026–27, including both 2022–23 Budgets | Budget aggregates; major economic parameters; domestic-economy forecasts; cash receipts; cash interest | Fiscal years 1998–99 to 2036–37 |
| MYEFO | 25 vintages, 2000–01 to 2025–26; no 2022–23 MYEFO was issued | Budget aggregates; Budget-comparator aggregates; major economic parameters; domestic-economy forecasts; cash receipts; cash interest | Fiscal years 1998–99 to 2035–36 |

These families cover fiscal balances, debt, aggregate receipts and payments;
GDP, inflation, wages, labour-market parameters; detailed domestic-economy
forecasts; individual receipt heads; and interest payments and receipts. MYEFO
Budget-comparator rows keep the preceding Budget forecast alongside the MYEFO
update.

The envelopes include future periods forecast in each publication; every
series and vintage has its own range. The panels retain Treasury tables for
domestic-economy forecasts, cash receipts, cash interest, and some MYEFO
aggregates and economic parameters. Selected normalized aggregate, comparator,
and economic rows come from the PBO's structured
[Historical budget forecasts and measures](https://www.pbo.gov.au/publications-and-data/data-and-tools/data-portal/historical-budget-forecasts-measures)
workbooks: Table 1 (*Medium term projections*), Table 2 (*Budget estimates*),
and Table 5 (*Economic forecasts*).

Table numbering changes across publication years. Use the stable
`table_family` to select content and `source_table` to identify the exact
published table. Each row's `actual_forecast` distinguishes realized values
from that vintage's projections, while `observation_source_url` and
`observation_source_sha256` identify the upstream observation product even
when the enclosing release remains a Treasury Budget or MYEFO.

Start with `list_au_budget_series()` or `list_au_myefo_series()` to inspect the
exact family, series, status, range, basis, unit, and source; then use
`read_au_budget()` or `read_au_myefo()` for one publication vintage.
`read_au_budget_history()` is a narrower cross-vintage reader for four audited
cash-receipts/accrual-revenue contracts, with actuals and forecasts kept
separate.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

This end-to-end example selects the pinned Treasury Budget 2024–25 release,
validates its official Table 1 resource contract, filters the returned curated
data to `Total receipts`, and charts the annual values in AUD billions.

The manifest pins the selected resource hash, and the returned provenance
records both the Table 1 CSV and Budget Paper 1 Table 5.7 observation sources.
The source attribution is © Commonwealth of Australia; consult the
[Treasury terms](https://budget.gov.au/legal-notices.htm#h1) before reusing the
values. The visible code makes a bounded live request, so CRAN and documentation
builds use the checked-in figure and remain deterministic and offline. Pass
exact bytes through `raw` or an injected `fetcher` for an offline replay.

```{r treasury-chart, eval=FALSE}
```

```{r treasury-chart-preview, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart of annual Australian Government total receipts from the Treasury Budget 2024–25 curated cash-receipts series, sourced from Table 1 and Budget Paper 1 Table 5.7, covering 2005–06 to 2027–28 in AUD billions."}
knitr::include_graphics("../man/figures/treasury-total-receipts.png")
```

Keep the full returned object and its `readfiscalau_provenance` attribute when
an analysis needs exact source bytes, terms, retrieval metadata, or cache
state. The chart does not imply Australian Government endorsement. The line
includes both published actual and forecast observations; retain
`actual_forecast` from the full result when that distinction matters.

## Compare historical Budget forecast vintages

The installed historical-table snapshot makes a cross-vintage chart local and
deterministic. This example selects every fourth Budget from 2004–05 through
2024–25, adds the latest 2026–27 Budget, and plots the underlying cash balance
from the GGS Budget aggregates as a share of GDP. This consistent forecast unit
is available in the admitted PDFs from 2004–05. The solid line adds the same
measure's annual actuals from PBO Historical Fiscal Data Table 1 over the
overlapping period; the selected Treasury Budget forecast paths remain dotted.

Each dotted line is the path printed in one Budget, rather than a revised
actual series. Both sources are installed snapshots, so no network request or
runtime PDF parsing is involved.

```{r budget-balance-vintages, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, out.width="100%", fig.alt="A solid line shows annual underlying cash balance actuals while dotted lines compare forecast paths published in seven selected Australian Budgets from 2004–05 to 2026–27, all measured as a percentage of GDP."}
```

The default reader keeps the canonical GGS aggregate occurrence for each
Budget-period combination. Set `all_sources = TRUE` when an audit needs the
same concept as printed in reconciliation, bridge, or formal-statement tables.

## Inspect the local catalogue

The manifest is local metadata. It distinguishes publication vintages and
resource updates; a row is not merely a reporting period.

```{r catalogue}
controls <- list_au_fiscal_search_controls()
head(controls)
```

```{r releases}
releases <- list_au_fiscal_releases(
  source = "treasury",
  release_type = "budget"
)
releases[, c("release_id", "release_type", "release_date",
             "release_status", "schema_family")][1:5, ]
```

The series catalogue functions provide a more exact local coverage view before
any source document is read:

```{r coverage}
budget_coverage <- list_au_budget_series()
budget_coverage[, c("release_id", "table_family", "series",
                    "actual_forecast", "start_date", "end_date")][1:5, ]
```

The full historical-table catalogue uses a separate, table-preserving
contract:

```{r historical-table-coverage}
table_coverage <- list_au_budget_myefo_tables(
  publication = "budget",
  release = "treasury-budget-2026-27-final"
)
table_coverage[, c(
  "family_label", "query_mode", "source_table", "source_page"
)][1:6, ]
```

## Read a small offline fixture

The example fixture is a small Treasury chart-data-shaped CSV packaged under
`inst/extdata/examples/`. The code starts from the packaged Budget CSV schema
contract and replaces the release/resource identity with an explicitly
synthetic fixture record before passing exact raw bytes to the real reader.
The values are for a schema/replay example; they are not presented as a
current official release.

```{r read-fixture}
# This block is standalone after installing and loading readfiscalau.
library(readfiscalau)
fixture_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "budget-current.csv", package = "readfiscalau"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(fixture_path), file.exists(fixture_path))
fixture_raw <- readBin(
  fixture_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(fixture_path)$size
)
fixture_release <- list_au_fiscal_releases(
  source = "treasury", release_type = "budget"
)
fixture_release <- fixture_release[
  fixture_release$schema_family == "treasury_chart_csv_v2", , drop = FALSE
][1, , drop = FALSE]
# Inherit the complete packaged 24-column contract, then identify the bytes as
# a synthetic fixture instead of claiming they are the selected release.
fixture_release[c(
  "release_id", "release_date", "period_end", "fiscal_year",
  "accounting_basis", "revision_semantics", "landing_url", "resource_id",
  "resource_role", "resource_url", "resource_updated_at", "expected_sha256"
)] <- list(
  "example-budget-2026-27", as.Date("2026-05-12"), as.Date("2027-06-30"),
  "2026-27", "mixed", "Small packaged chart-data-shaped example fixture.",
  "https://budget.gov.au/content/downloads.htm", "example-budget-chart-data",
  "example_chart_csv", "https://budget.gov.au/content/download/chart-data-final.csv",
  "2026-05-12T07:36:13Z", NA_character_
)
data <- read_au_budget(
  fixture_release,
  raw = fixture_raw,
  cache_dir = tempfile("readfiscalau-example-cache-")
)
data[, c("series", "fiscal_year", "period_end", "value", "unit",
         "actual_forecast", "release_id")]
```

The result is a `readfiscalau_data` tibble. Release and source fields are
included in the rows, and the provenance attribute retains the exact source
bytes and cache metadata:

```{r provenance}
provenance <- attr(data, "readfiscalau_provenance")
list(
  class = class(data),
  release_id = provenance$release$release_id,
  raw_content_sha256 = provenance$raw_content_sha256,
  cache_hit = provenance$cache_hit,
  schema_version = provenance$schema_version,
  terms_url = provenance$terms_url
)
```

The fixture uses one Treasury-shaped source, so its release-level terms and
observation source coincide. In curated Budget/MYEFO panels they can differ:
`license`, `terms_url`, `attribution`, and `raw_content_sha256` describe the
selected release/resource, while the coverage rows
`observation_source_url` and `observation_source_sha256` identify the upstream
product for the particular table/series/status. A PBO URL means the PBO
CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 caveat applies to those observations; Treasury release terms
do not license PBO-derived observations.

When a chart-data ZIP contains more than one CSV table, select the member
explicitly. The packaged ZIP fixture exercises that branch without a network
call:

```{r zip-table}
zip_release <- example_budget_release()
zip_release$resource_url <-
  "https://budget.gov.au/content/download/chart-data-final.zip"
zip_release$resource_role <- "example_chart_zip"
zip_release$media_type <- "application/zip"
zip_release$schema_family <- "treasury_chart_zip_csv_v2"
zip_data <- read_au_budget(
  zip_release,
  raw = example_raw("budget-chart-archive.zip"),
  table_id = "Table 1",
  cache_dir = tempfile("readfiscalau-zip-cache-")
)
c(
  rows = nrow(zip_data),
  archive_member = attr(zip_data, "readfiscalau_provenance")$archive_member$name
)
```

For a live read, pass a release ID from `list_au_fiscal_releases()` to the
matching typed reader and omit `raw`. That call uses HTTPS, validates the
selected source contract and expected hash, and writes to the bounded user
cache. It is intentionally not executed in this vignette.

```r
live_budget <- read_au_budget(releases$release_id[[1]])
```

## Where to go next

- Use `release-catalogues.Rmd` to separate discovery candidates from the
  curated manifest and inspect Finance CKAN resource vintages.
- Use `provenance-and-cache.Rmd` to replay bytes offline and inspect cache-hit
  behavior.
- Use `read_au_budget_history()` for actual/forecast vintage comparisons and
  `read_au_monthly_financial_history()` for Finance monthly/YTD history.
- Use `budget-myefo-table-history.Rmd` for the 22-family static PDF-table
  snapshot, canonical series deduplication, and complete-table retrieval.
- Use `budget-archive.Rmd` before running any durable Budget-document archive
  operation.
- Use `troubleshooting.Rmd` for typed conditions and source/schema failures.
